```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.pos = 'h',
                      fig.height = 3, fig.width = 4, fig.align = "center")
library(rcycle)
## the development version, if the installed one is older
if ( !"phase_time" %in% getNamespaceExports("rcycle") )
    devtools::load_all("~/programs/rcycle", quiet=TRUE)
script <- system.file("scripts", "jackson20_phasetime.R", package="rcycle")
if ( script=="" )
    script <- "~/programs/rcycle/inst/scripts/jackson20_phasetime.R"
```

How long do cells spend in each phase of the division cycle, and how
variable is that? From a snapshot of an asynchronous, exponentially
growing population, ergodic rate analysis [ERA, @Kafri2013] converts the
order of the cells along the cycle into time: a cell with a fraction
`F` of all cells between division and itself has the age
`T*(1-log2(2-F))`, `T` the doubling time (see `ROADMAP.md`). Young
cells are more frequent than old ones, so the linear calibration of the
rank phase (`calibrate`) overestimates early ages.

We use the 11 media of @Jackson2020 and the growth rates of the
owner's pipeline. The phase comes from all periodic Cyclebase genes in
five peak-time bins (`cdc_bins_*`, 3080 genes); the landmarks are the
peaks of the full division-cycle cohorts of @Spellman1998 (M/G1, G1, S,
G2, M) along it. Removing the genes of the growth cohorts and of
HOC/LOC from the Spellman cohorts (the pipeline's `cdc_*`) loses most
cycling genes, halves the reproducibility of the phase and puts the
cohorts in the wrong order in several media (`ROADMAP.md`).

```{r run, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cdc <- c("cdc_M/G1", "cdc_G1", "cdc_S", "cdc_G2", "cdc_M")
outfile <- tempfile(fileext=".rda")
source(script)
```


# From cohort states to age, step by step

```{r steps, fig.cap="From cohort states to age, YPD. A: cells (PCA loadings, each cell scaled to unit variance) in the PC1/PC2 plane, colored by ERA age; arrows: directions of the five Cyclebase cohorts; grey circles: noise cells; red: the angle theta of one cell. B: the same cells at their unscaled amplitude in the plane: noise cells fall to the center. C: the angle against the rank phase, the order of the cells along the cycle; steep where cells pass quickly, flat where they accumulate. D: the ERA transform of the fraction of cells since division into age (red), against the linear calibration (grey), and the density of ages. E: the full Spellman cohorts along age, with peaks and points of maximal change on the top axis; shaded: G1, S, G2/M.", fig.width=7, fig.height=9.5}
P <- R$YPD$P
labs <- paste("bin", 1:5)
layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.35,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plotPhasePlane(P, labels=labs)
mtext("A", 3, .5, adj=0, font=2)
plotPhasePlane(P, raw=TRUE, labels=labs, example=NA)
mtext("B", 3, .5, adj=0, font=2)
plotPhaseOrder(P)
mtext("C", 3, 1.3, adj=0, font=2)
plotEra(P)
mtext("D", 3, .5, adj=0, font=2)
plotAgeStates(P, marks(J$jackson20_YPD), R$YPD$durations,
              shade=c("cdc_M/G1", "G1S", "SG2"), xlab="age, h")
mtext("E", 3, 1.3, adj=0, font=2)
```

# Methods

## Cohort states and the pseudophase

For cell $j$ with total count $N_j$ and gene counts $c_{gj}$, the state
of cohort $k$ with $n_k$ genes is the mean fraction per gene,
$s_{kj} = \frac{1}{n_k}\sum_{g\in k} c_{gj}/N_j$ (`get_states`). The
cohort x cell matrix is centered per cohort (row means over cells),
then each cell (column) is centered and scaled to unit variance, and
decomposed by PCA, $Z = X V^\top$ (`get_pseudophase`, with
`stats::prcomp`): the cohorts are the samples, with scores $X$, the
cells the variables, with loadings $V$. A cell's phase angle is the
angle of its loadings in the plane of the first two PCs,
$\theta_j = \operatorname{atan2}(V_{j2}, V_{j1})$, and its rank phase
spreads the cells evenly over the circle,
$\phi_j = 2\pi\,\operatorname{rank}(\theta_j)/n - \pi$. The direction is
set by the order of the cohorts.

## Ergodic rate analysis: from order to age

In an asynchronous population growing exponentially at rate
$\alpha = \ln 2/T$, the distribution of cells along the cycle path
$\ell$ does not change; let $f(\ell)$ be the density of cells and
$F(\ell)=\int_0^\ell f$ the fraction between division ($\ell=0$) and
$\ell$. With $N$ cells, divisions occur at rate $\alpha N$ (each adds one
cell), so $2\alpha N$ newborn cells enter at $\ell = 0$ per time. The flux
of cells through $\ell$, $J(\ell) = v(\ell) N f(\ell)$ with speed $v$, is
the inflow minus what accumulates before $\ell$,
$J(\ell) = 2\alpha N - \frac{d}{dt}(N F) = \alpha N (2 - F)$, so
[@Kafri2013, Box 2]
$$
v(\ell) = \alpha\,\frac{2 - F(\ell)}{f(\ell)}\,, \qquad
a(\ell) = \int_0^\ell \frac{d\ell'}{v(\ell')}
        = \frac{1}{\alpha}\int_0^{F} \frac{dF'}{2-F'}
        = T\left(1 - \log_2\left(2-F\right)\right)\,.
$$
Only the order of the cells enters, through $F$: the age of a cell
(`era_age`, `phase_time`) follows from its rank, $F_j = (\mathrm{rank}_j
- 1/2)/n$, counted from the origin in the direction of the phase. The
ages have the density $p(a) = 2\alpha\,e^{-\alpha a}$ on $[0, T]$:
young cells are twice as frequent as the oldest, which the linear
calibration $a = F\,T$ ignores. The duration between two landmarks is
the difference of their ages (`phase_durations`).

A group of cells that receives a share $s$ of the newborn cells
($s=1/2$ for mothers or daughters) and holds a fraction $f$ of all
cells in a phase that starts at division and lasts $\tau$ obeys
$f = 2s\,(1 - e^{-\alpha\tau})$, so (`era_duration`, `group_durations`)
$$
\tau = -T \log_2\left(1 - \frac{f}{2s}\right)\,,
$$
which is $a(F)$ for $s = 1$.

## Landmarks

A cohort peak is the maximum of the moving average of the cohort state
over 5% of the cells, sorted by phase (`state_phase`). A point of
maximal change between two peaks is where the cell angle changes
fastest per cell: the maximum, on the arc between the peaks, of
$\frac{d}{d\phi}(\theta - \phi)$ from a penalized spline of
$\theta - \phi$ against $\phi$ (`get_segments`, `phase_landmarks`).
The width of a peak is the age span over which the scaled moving
average is at least one half.

## Per-cell quality

New cells, with states $s_{\cdot j}$, are projected into an existing
PCA with its preprocessing: subtract the original cohort means, center
and scale the column, $z_j$, and, since the score vectors $x_k$ are
orthogonal with $\lVert x_k \rVert^2 = (m-1)\sigma_k^2$ ($m$ cohorts,
$\sigma_k$ the PC standard deviations), the loadings are
$r_{jk} = x_k^\top z_j / ((m-1)\sigma_k^2)$ (`project_cells`; exact for
the original cells). The share of the cell's variance in the PC1/PC2
plane is $r^2_j = \sum_{k\le 2}\sigma_k^2 r_{jk}^2 / \sum_k \sigma_k^2
r_{jk}^2$, and its unscaled amplitude in that plane is
$A_j = \mathrm{sd}_j\sqrt{r^2_j}$, with $\mathrm{sd}_j$ the cell's
standard deviation across cohorts before scaling.

The noise reference (`noise_states`) draws, for each cell, cohort
counts without a cycle, $S_{kj} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(N_j p_k)$, with
the population fraction of each cohort's reads
$p_k = \sum_j n_k s_{kj} N_j / \sum_j N_j$, and converts them to states
$S_{kj}/(n_k N_j)$. With $B$ such noise cells per cell, projected into
the same PCA, the p-value is $(1 + \#\{b: A_b \ge A_j\})/(B+1)$; cells
with $p > 0.05$ are flagged as noise (`cell_quality`; $B \ge 20$).

The phase uncertainty of a cell (`phase_bootstrap`) comes from
resampling the genes of each cohort with replacement, recomputing the
states and projecting: the spread of the cell's rank fraction $F$ over
resamples, $\sigma_F$, gives the spread of its age by the derivative of
the ERA transform, $\sigma_a = \sigma_F\,T/((2-F)\ln 2)$.

## Closed principal curve

`principal_phase` fits a closed curve
$\gamma(\lambda) = c_0 + \sum_{m=1}^{K} (a_m \cos m\lambda + b_m \sin m\lambda)$
through the cells' loadings in the first $k$ PCs (each scaled by
$\sigma_k$), starting at $\lambda = \theta$, and alternates least
squares fits of the coefficients with projecting each cell to the
nearest point of the curve, with $\lambda$ the arc length scaled to
$2\pi$ [@Hastie1989].

## Daughter calls

`split_counts` fits the counts $x_j$ of a cohort as a mixture of two
Poisson distributions with rates proportional to the total,
$x_j \sim \pi_1\,\mathrm{Pois}(r_1 N_j) + \pi_2\,\mathrm{Pois}(r_2 N_j)$,
by expectation maximization; cells with posterior $>1/2$ for the higher
rate are called.


# One medium: YPD

```{r ypd}
r <- R$YPD
P <- r$P
rp <- P$rotation.phase
r$T
r$durations
```

The origin (division) is the moving-average peak of the M/G1 cohort.
`G1S` is the point of maximal change of the cell angle between the G1
and the S cohort peaks, `SG2` and `G2M` likewise (`phase_landmarks`,
from the inflection segmentation of `get_segments`).

```{r ypd-states, fig.cap="Left: cohort states (moving average over 5% of the cells) along the ERA age; top axis: cohort peaks and points of maximal change. Right: ERA age against the linear calibration of the rank phase, F*T (grey: identity).", fig.width=7}
st <- marks(J$jackson20_YPD)
ord <- order(rp$age)
ma <- t(apply(st[, ord], 1, function(x)
    stats::filter(x, rep(1, 500)/500, circular=TRUE)))
ma <- ma/apply(ma, 1, max)
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.3,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
matplot(rp$age[ord], t(ma), type='l', lty=1, col=1:5,
        xlab="age, h", ylab="state / max")
axis(3, at=r$durations$age, labels=sub("cdc_", "", r$durations$landmark),
     las=2, cex.axis=.7)
legend("bottomleft", sub("cdc_", "", cdc), col=1:5, lty=1, cex=.7,
       bty='n')
plot(rp$age_F*r$T, rp$age, pch=".", xlab="linear, F*T (h)",
     ylab="ERA age (h)")
abline(0, 1, col="grey")
```

## Per-cell quality

With `scale=TRUE` each cell has unit variance across cohorts.
`cell_quality` recovers the unscaled amplitude in the PC1/PC2 plane and
compares it with 20 noise cells per cell, drawn from Poisson counts of
the same totals without a cycle (`noise_states`).

```{r ypd-quality, fig.cap="Unscaled amplitude against total counts; red: not above the noise reference (p > 0.05), grey: noise cells.", fig.width=7}
nz <- P$noise
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(J$jackson20_YPD$total[nz$cell], nz$amplitude.raw, pch=".",
     col="grey", log="xy", xlab="total counts",
     ylab="amplitude (unscaled)")
points(J$jackson20_YPD$total, rp$amplitude.raw, pch=".",
       col=ifelse(rp$noise, 2, 1))
hist(rp$r2, breaks=50, main=NA, xlab="variance share in PC1/PC2")
mean(rp$noise)
```

A cell's phase also depends on which genes represent its cohorts.
`phase_bootstrap` resamples genes within cohorts:

```{r ypd-boot}
summary(rp$F.sd)   # fraction of the cycle
summary(rp$age.sd) # hours
```

## Size along age

The log total count is a proxy of cell size (and of capture
efficiency). If size is controlled at G1 exit, its spread should narrow
there. In YPD the mean is lowest from G1 to S and the spread is
narrowest around the G2 peak, not at G1 exit.

```{r ypd-size, fig.cap="Mean and standard deviation of log total counts along age; vertical lines: landmarks."}
pr <- age_profile(rp$age, log(J$jackson20_YPD$total), breaks=20)
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.5), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(pr$mid, pr$mean, type='b', xlab="age, h", ylab="mean log total")
abline(v=r$durations$age, col="grey")
par(new=TRUE)
plot(pr$mid, pr$sd, type='b', col=2, axes=FALSE, xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
axis(4, col=2, col.axis=2)
mtext("sd log total", 4, 1.3, col=2)
```

## Daughters and mothers

`split_counts` calls daughter cells by a two-component Poisson mixture
of the counts of the daughter cohort. The fraction of daughter calls
along age shows that this cohort is expressed in nearly all cells
around division, so it marks the M/G1 stage, not daughters alone; the
group durations (`group_durations`) are therefore not yet meaningful.

```{r ypd-daughter, fig.cap="Fraction of cells called daughter along age."}
pd <- age_profile(rp$age, as.numeric(r$daughter$high), breaks=20)
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(pd$mid, pd$mean, type='b', xlab="age, h", ylab="daughter calls")
r$groups$G1S
```

# G1 against doubling time

```{r media}
tab[, c("medium", "T", "cells", "noise", "order.ok", "G1.S", "G1.G1S",
        "G1.G1S.clean")]
```

`order.ok`: the cohort peaks are in cycle order from M/G1. Where they
are not, the landmarks mix phases (e.g. M after M/G1), and the G1
durations are not G1.

```{r media-plot, fig.cap="G1 share of the doubling time, origin at the M/G1 peak, to the point of maximal change (G1S, filled, with 95% intervals from resampling cells, `duration_ci`) or the S peak (open), without noise cells; red: cohort order wrong. Spearman correlations for the 9 growing media and for those in correct order."}
g <- !is.na(tab$T) & tab$mu > .1
x <- tab[g,]
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(x$T, x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, pch=19, col=ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2),
     ylim=c(0, .6), xlim=c(1, 2.3), xlab="doubling time, h",
     ylab="G1 / T")
points(x$T, x$G1.S.clean/x$T, col=ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2))
arrows(x$T, x$G1.lo/x$T, x$T, x$G1.hi/x$T, angle=90, code=3,
       length=.02, col=ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2))
text(x$T, x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, x$medium, pos=4, cex=.5, xpd=TRUE)
sp <- function(y, i=TRUE) round(cor(x$T[i], y[i], method="spearman"), 2)
c(all=sp(x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T), order.ok=sp(x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, x$order.ok))
```

# S and G2 against doubling time

S lasts from `G1S` to `SG2`, G2 from `SG2` to `G2M`; peak to peak
intervals (S to G2 peak) are more robust than the points of maximal
change between S, G2 and M, which jump between media. The width of a
cohort peak is the full width at half maximum of its moving average
along age; it includes the per-cell phase uncertainty, so it is an
upper bound and not the cell-to-cell spread of a phase duration.

```{r phases}
v <- c(G1="G1.G1S.clean", S="S.clean", G2="G2.clean",
       "S-G2 peaks"="SG2pk.clean", "S width"="wS.clean",
       "G2 width"="wG2.clean")
round(sapply(v, function(i) c(
    hours=cor(x$T, x[[i]], method="spearman"),
    share=cor(x$T, x[[i]]/x$T, method="spearman"),
    min=min(x[[i]]/x$T), max=max(x[[i]]/x$T))), 2)
```

```{r phases-plot, fig.cap="Left: S (G1S to SG2, filled, with 95% intervals from resampling cells) and the S peak width (open) in hours; right: as share of the doubling time. Red: cohort order wrong.", fig.width=7}
col <- ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2)
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(x$T, x$S.clean, pch=19, col=col, ylim=c(0, .6),
     xlab="doubling time, h", ylab="S, h")
arrows(x$T, x$S.lo, x$T, x$S.hi, angle=90, code=3, length=.02, col=col)
points(x$T, x$wS.clean, col=col)
plot(x$T, x$S.clean/x$T, pch=19, col=col, ylim=c(0, .4),
     xlab="doubling time, h", ylab="S / T")
arrows(x$T, x$S.lo/x$T, x$T, x$S.hi/x$T, angle=90, code=3, length=.02,
       col=col)
points(x$T, x$wS.clean/x$T, col=col)
```

S takes about the same time in all media, so its share of the cycle,
and the width of the histone peak relative to T, fall in slower media;
G1 and the S-to-G2 peak interval scale with T.

# Growth cohorts along age

To read a growth cohort against the division cycle, its genes are left
out of the phase (`division_phase(..., exclude=)`), so that the phase
cannot follow the cohort itself. Along the ERA age, the cells of a
snapshot are not evenly spread: young cells are twice as frequent as
the oldest. The average over a cell's cycle weights each cell by
`2^(age/T)` (`time_weights`, `time_mean`); the snapshot mean over
cells over-weights early G1.

```{r growth, results='hide', message=FALSE}
x <- J$jackson20_YPD
gc <- c("cgc_Ribi", "cgc_RP", "cgc_AA", "cgc_mRP", "cgc_S/C")
coh <- x$cohorts[phase.cohorts]
mks <- setNames(x$cohorts[mark.cohorts], cdc)
G <- lapply(setNames(gc, gc), function(k) {
    Pk <- division_phase(x$counts, x$total, coh, mks, T=R$YPD$T,
                         between=between, exclude=x$cohorts[[k]],
                         noise.rm=TRUE, seed=1)
    y <- cohort_states(x$counts[, Pk$cells], x$total[Pk$cells],
                       x$cohorts[k])[1,]
    list(P=Pk, y=y/mean(y))
})
```

```{r growth-tab}
round(t(sapply(G, function(g) {
    a <- g$P$rotation.phase$age
    g1 <- a < g$P$durations$age[g$P$durations$landmark=="G1S"]
    hi <- g$y > median(g$y)
    c(order.ok=g$P$order.ok, G1=max(a[g1]),
      high.snapshot=mean(hi), high.time=time_mean(hi, a, R$YPD$T),
      G1.snapshot=mean(g$y[g1]),
      G1.time=time_mean(g$y[g1], a[g1], R$YPD$T))
})), 3)
```

`high`: share of cells (snapshot) or of the cycle (time) with the
cohort above its median; `G1`: the G1 duration (h) of the phase
without the cohort's genes, and the cohort's mean in G1 (relative to
all cells), over G1 cells or over the time of G1.

```{r growth-plot, fig.cap="Growth cohorts along age in YPD, each against a phase without its genes: moving average over 5% of the cells, relative to the cohort mean; vertical lines: landmarks of the Ribi phase.", fig.width=7}
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.3,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(1, type='n', xlim=c(0, R$YPD$T), ylim=c(.6, 1.4), xlab="age, h",
     ylab="state / mean")
d <- G$cgc_Ribi$P$durations
abline(v=d$age, col="grey", lwd=.5)
axis(3, at=d$age, labels=sub("cdc_", "", d$landmark), las=2,
     cex.axis=.7)
for ( i in seq_along(G) ) {
    a <- G[[i]]$P$rotation.phase$age
    o <- order(a)
    n <- round(.05*length(a))
    lines(a[o], stats::filter(G[[i]]$y[o], rep(1, n)/n, circular=TRUE),
          col=i, lwd=1.5)
}
legend("topright", sub("cgc_", "", names(G)), col=seq_along(G),
       lty=1, lwd=1.5, cex=.7, bty='n')
```

# Nadal-Ribelles et al. 2025

Two deep sets of 10,000 cells: exponential growth in YPD (`ctrl`), and
15 min after 0.4 M NaCl (`nacl`), not a steady state, so ERA does not
strictly apply. The growth rate is not known, so ages are in units of
the cycle. The cohort states are computed from the counts with the
same gene lists.

```{r nadal, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
nscript <- sub("jackson20", "nadal25", script)
nad <- new.env()
assign("outfile", tempfile(fileext=".rda"), envir=nad)
source(nscript, local=nad)
```

```{r nadal-tab}
nad$tab[, c("medium", "cells", "noise", "order.ok", "G1.G1S.clean",
            "S.clean", "SG2pk.clean", "wS.clean")]
nad$R$`ctrl-high`$durations[, c("landmark", "age", "duration")]
```

In the control, G1 takes 0.12 and S 0.21 of the cycle, close to YPD in
@Jackson2020 (0.13 and 0.18 of T). After NaCl, G1 takes a larger share.

The published classes (G1, S, G2M) along age: their S class agrees with
the S peak; their G1 class covers both the first part of the cycle
and much of its second half, where G2M cells should be. G1 may there be
the class of cells without a clear S or G2M signal.

```{r nadal-classes, fig.cap="Fraction of the published classes along age, Nadal-Ribelles 2025, control and NaCl; vertical lines: landmarks.", fig.width=7}
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.3,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
for ( id in names(nad$R) ) {
    rp <- nad$R[[id]]$P$rotation.phase
    cl <- nad$cls[[id]]
    pr <- sapply(c("G1", "S", "G2M"), function(k)
        age_profile(rp$age, as.numeric(cl==k), breaks=20)$mean)
    a <- age_profile(rp$age, rp$age, breaks=20)$mid
    matplot(a, pr, type='l', lty=1, col=1:3, ylim=c(0, 1),
            xlab="age / cycle", ylab="fraction of cells", main=id)
    abline(v=nad$R[[id]]$durations$age, col="grey", lwd=.5)
    legend("top", c("G1", "S", "G2M"), col=1:3, lty=1, cex=.7, bty='n',
           horiz=TRUE)
}
```

# References
